title: Japan Orders Mass Evacuations as Typhoon Dolphin Cancels Over 500 Flights
excerpt: The Category 1 storm is bearing down on southwestern Japan with 144 kph winds, forcing 260,000 to evacuate and shuttering Toyota factories. China's eastern coast braces for landfall within days.
body:
• Typhoon Dolphin has prompted evacuation orders for nearly 260,000 residents across Kagoshima and Okinawa prefectures in southwestern Japan.
  • More than 500 flights have been cancelled and Toyota has suspended operations at nine factories.
  • The storm is hitting Kumamoto prefecture, where 6,700 residents are still in evacuation centres after last week's magnitude 7.1 earthquake.
  • Dolphin is expected to make landfall along China's eastern coast between Shanghai and Fujian around August 9-10, potentially disrupting major ports.

Hundreds of thousands of people in southwestern Japan were ordered to evacuate on Friday as slow-moving Typhoon Dolphin bore down on the region, cancelling more than 500 flights, shuttering factories and threatening further misery for communities still recovering from last week's deadly earthquake.

The Category 1 typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 144 kilometres per hour with gusts reaching 198 kph as it neared a chain of islands between the Kyushu region and Okinawa prefecture, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

Evacuations and Factory Shutdowns

Authorities issued evacuation orders for nearly 260,000 residents in Kagoshima and Okinawa prefectures. Toyota suspended operations at nine factories across the region on Friday, adding to an already difficult period for Japanese manufacturers navigating supply chain disruptions.

The weather agency warned that Dolphin could maintain its strength as it approached Okinawa, raising the risk of winds powerful enough to damage or collapse structures. A linear rain band — a narrow belt of intense precipitation and thunderstorms — could also develop, potentially triggering flash flooding.

Double Blow for Quake-Hit Kumamoto

The storm's path carries particular risk for Kumamoto prefecture on the main island of Kyushu, which is still reeling from a magnitude 7.1 earthquake last week. Some 6,700 Kumamoto residents remain in evacuation centres after many houses collapsed in the quake. The combination of a powerful typhoon and weakened structures raises the danger of secondary collapses.

Authorities have also warned of heatstroke risks, with temperatures expected to reach 36 degrees Celsius in some areas — a hazard for evacuees without adequate shelter or cooling.

"Evacuations and Factory Shutdowns Authorities issued evacuation orders for nearly 260,000 residents in Kagoshima and Okinawa prefectures."

China Braces for Impact

After passing through Japan, Typhoon Dolphin is expected to make landfall along China's eastern coast — somewhere between Shanghai and Fujian province — around August 9-10, according to Chinese meteorological authorities. The storm is forecast to bring heavy rainfall and strong winds to one of the world's busiest shipping corridors.

China is already dealing with severe weather. More than 140,000 people have been evacuated in the northwestern province of Shaanxi since July 30 due to heavy rains and flooding that collapsed roads and damaged bridges and power infrastructure. Northern China could face even heavier rainfall after Dolphin makes landfall and interacts with cold air systems, authorities warned.

Travel Disruptions to Watch

For travellers with plans in Japan or eastern China, the disruptions are significant. Airlines have grounded more than 500 domestic and regional flights, with further cancellations expected through the weekend. Ferry services to Okinawa and the southern islands are suspended, and rail services in Kyushu face delays and cancellations.

Indian nationals and diaspora travellers in the region should monitor airline advisories closely. Japan's peak summer travel season means rebooking options are limited, and hotel accommodations in unaffected areas are filling up quickly. Those with travel plans to Shanghai or eastern China in the coming days should prepare for port closures and potential flight disruptions as Dolphin makes its way across the East China Sea.
